objectives: Describe the parts of the CybICS gas plant and what each actuator does to the tanks
Explain how the automatic mode keeps the high-pressure tank in its normal band
Predict how the pressure changes when an operator switches actuators in manual mode
Name ways a defender notices and limits unsafe manual control
takeaways: In manual mode the PLC stops deciding, and whoever controls the HMI buttons controls the physical process.
The compressor trades two units of storage gas for one unit of pressure, so the storage tank limits how far it can push.
The blowout valve is a latch: it opens above 220, vents until 200 and then closes again.
Process monitoring catches unsafe states no matter whether an operator or an attacker caused them.
Independent safety functions and least privilege on the HMI limit what a stolen operator login can do.

checkpoints.question: The compressor runs and the storage tank starts full at about 242. Nothing refills it. Roughly how much pressure can the compressor add to the HPT?
options: About 121 units
About 97 units
About 192 units
checkpoints.explanation: Each transfer costs two units of storage for one unit of pressure, and it stops once storage falls below 50. From 242 down to 48 that is 97 transfers. Halving 242 to 121 forgets the guard at 50, and 192 (242 minus 50) forgets that the exchange rate is two to one. The compressor only moves what the storage tank holds.

quiz.question: What changes when the operator switches the FUXA HMI from automatic to manual mode?
options: The PLC shuts down and the plant stops
The PLC stops deciding; the buttons write the coils
The blowout valve comes under the operator's control
The sensors stop updating until automatic mode returns
quiz.explanation: In manual mode the PLC program skips its control rules, so the coils keep whatever the operator writes. The plant keeps running and the sensors keep reporting. The blowout valve is the tempting wrong answer: it is mechanical and independent, so neither manual mode nor any button can control it.

quiz.question: In automatic mode, when does the PLC open the system valve?
options: Whenever the compressor is switched off
While the HPT reads between 50 and 100
While the HPT reads between 60 and 90
Only while the GST is being refilled from outside
quiz.explanation: The program opens the system valve while the HPT reads above 50 and below 100. The band from 60 to 90 belongs to the compressor, which starts below 60 and stops at 90; it is easy to mix the two up. The valve rule does not look at the compressor or the GST.

quiz.question: The plant is in manual mode, the HPT has passed 220 and the blowout valve is venting, but the compressor is still running. What happens?
options: The valve holds the pressure at exactly 220
It keeps rising; the valve vents slower than it fills
The PLC switches the compressor off as soon as the valve opens
It falls back to 200, where the valve closes again
quiz.explanation: The valve vents about half a bar per tick against the compressor's one bar, so a compressor that keeps running still wins. The valve is not a ceiling. In manual mode the PLC does not intervene, so nothing switches the compressor off when the valve opens.

quiz.question: After a blowout the compressor is off and the system valve is shut. Where does the HPT pressure settle?
options: Back in the normal band of 60 to 90
At about 200, where the valve closes
At 0, because the valve keeps venting
Just below 220, where the valve opened
quiz.explanation: The relief valve is a latch: it opens above 220, stays open until the pressure is back at 200 and then closes. It does not close at 220 and it does not keep venting below 200. With the compressor off and the system valve shut, nothing else drains the tank, so it does not return to the normal band on its own.

quiz.question: Which measures help a defender against unsafe manual control from the HMI? (Select all that apply)
options: Alarming when the HPT leaves its normal band
Giving only some accounts permission to use manual mode
Keeping the safety relief independent of the PLC and the HMI
Encrypting the connection between the HMI and the PLC
quiz.explanation: Process alarms catch the effect, role-based permissions limit who can cause it, and an independent safety function limits the damage. Encryption protects the messages on the wire, but here the unsafe commands come from a logged-in operator, so they would be encrypted and delivered just the same.
